html:
Unreal actor and component property automation

ForgeMCP exposes three actor-property operations on a connected Unreal Editor:

  • unreal_inspect_actor_properties reads bounded simple reflected values from one loaded level actor and reports whether each field is editable in the current Editor context.
  • unreal_preview_actor_property_edit validates one proposed native property-text value and returns the current and proposed values.
  • unreal_apply_actor_property_edit applies that single-use preview to the same actor and property after rechecking actor, class, world, current value and editability.

The component equivalents target one exact loaded actor component:

  • unreal_inspect_component_properties returns a bounded page of simple reflected values and Editor editability metadata.
  • unreal_preview_component_property_edit validates one proposed native property-text value and binds it to the exact component, owner, class, world and prior value.
  • unreal_apply_component_property_edit applies the single-use preview after rechecking that identity and prior value.

Supported values are scalar numerics, booleans, byte/enums, names, strings, text, vectors, rotators and colors. Arrays and nested objects are not traversed. Property names are exact reflected identifiers; the adapter uses Unreal's own FProperty parser and CanEditChange check. Apply records an Editor transaction, emits property-change notifications, verifies the resulting value, marks the level dirty and does not save it. Saving the level remains a separate, explicit operation. Editability metadata does not guarantee every text representation is accepted by Unreal's property parser; preview reports parser rejection before mutation. Native bitfield booleans are handled through FBoolProperty and accept true/false or 1/0, then normalize to Unreal's lowercase boolean export.

Inspection and edit scope is the loaded actor instance in the current Editor world. Play-in-Editor and stale actor/world/property previews are rejected. This does not provide arbitrary UObject references, container traversal, batch edits, disk backups or automatic level saving. Only components owned by actors in the current loaded Editor world can be resolved.

The native MCP acceptance fixture uses an actor spawned only in a disposable UE 5.6.1 project. It queried the actual editable numeric fields, applied one property change, read it back through MCP and rejected a competing stale preview. This is headless native acceptance; interactive Details-panel refresh and actual Undo behavior still need visible Editor verification.
